perspective:
Keith Ndiaye’s available information:

- Keith works as a construction worker at the same company where Elizabeth Sun is the receptionist. They have a friendly but professional colleague relationship, usually interacting when Keith visits the office for paperwork or project updates.
- Recently, Keith observed Elizabeth being unusually curt or short with him over several days. He wondered whether he had upset her through a misunderstanding or an unknowing mistake.
- Keith asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. He heard Elizabeth say she was not upset with him, that she was dealing with personal stuff, and that she was sorry if she seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic and wanted to support her. He offered to listen and suggested a coffee break. He heard Elizabeth accept, saying it was kind and that coffee sounded good.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses, which Keith perceived as serious. Keith thanked her for sharing and asked whether she had considered talking to a professional, saying an external perspective can sometimes help. He heard Elizabeth say she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant about seeking help.
- After the suggestion, Keith noticed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn. He thought his suggestion might have embarrassed her and felt regretful. He told her he hoped he had not overstepped, and that he wanted her to know he was there to support her. He heard Elizabeth say he had not overstepped, that she appreciated his concern, and that it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith perceived Elizabeth as more open and appreciative of his concern. He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him. He told her he was glad they talked and that he was always available if she needed to chat or take a break. He heard Elizabeth thank him, say it meant a lot, and say she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith intends to maintain this supportive relationship with Elizabeth.
